The two small eigenvalues, in the accent color, stand well apart from the rest, matching the two triangle communities." width="100%"} The eigenvalues of `bethe_hessian_matrix()`, in increasing order. On large sparse networks, the number of negative eigenvalues at a suitable `r` (Saade et al. recommend the square root of the default) estimates the number of communities. At `r = 1` the spectrum is the Laplacian spectrum. Matches NetworkX's `bethe_hessian_spectrum()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [r]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The regularizer. If `None` (default), uses `Σ d² / Σ d - 1`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The eigenvalues in increasing order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, or `r=` is omitted on a graph without edges. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The spectrum at the default `r`, and at `r = 1`, where its smallest value is the Laplacian's `0`: ::: {#bda7b8a8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes(list("ABCDEF")) graph.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ( [round(v, 3) for v in graph.bethe_hessian_spectrum()], [round(v, 3) for v in graph.bethe_hessian_spectrum(r=1)], ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ([0.031, 0.748, 4.194, 4.469, 4.469, 6.334], [0.0, 0.438, 3.0, 3.0, 3.0, 4.562]) ``` ::: :::
